title: AI did not delete Swedish reality TV series, broadcaster says
key_facts: Swedish broadcaster TV4 has rejected reports that an AI agent deleted an entire edited season of a TV show weeks before it was due to air.

Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet first reported, citing sources, that production company Mastiff gave an AI agent access to its servers and it deleted the edited second season of the reality show The Challenge Sverige.
The sources said the files are unrecoverable and the season must be re-edited, which reportedly took a year the first time.
A spokesperson for the show confirmed the files disappeared and that the premiere moves from 22 Nov to some time next year, but did not confirm AI involvement, citing only a technical breakdown.
TV4 programme director Mia Lindqvist told Aftonbladet that the main problem was a failed backup, and that TV4's investigation found human error with no AI involved.
Lindqvist said most production companies now use AI, but here it was apparently not to blame.
quote_evidence: TV4's program director Mia Lindqvist subsequently denied that AI was responsible for the mishap, telling Aftonbladet in a later statement that the primary problem was that a backup had failed.
An investigation by TV4 had found that The Challenge's edited second season had been deleted due to human error, with no AI involved.
However, said spokesperson did not confirm AI involvement, saying only that there was a technical breakdown.
why_it_matters_hint: The claim that an AI agent wiped a TV season is now denied by the broadcaster, leaving the cause as human error and a failed backup.
event_date: Deletion reported by Aftonbladet on 14 Oct 2026; TV4 denial reported by Mashable on 17 Oct 2026
notes: Follow-up of the 16 Oct 2026 edition entry 103, which already carried TV4's denial, the failed backup and the delay of the 22 Nov premiere. Little is new today beyond the spokesperson saying only technical breakdown and Lindqvist's remark on AI use. Mashable is the relay; Aftonbladet is the original reporter.
